papers.abstract: <jats:p>An early distinction between the early and reversible changes of cellular ischemia and the irreversible changes of cell necrosis is essential to a rational program for the treatment of coronary artery disease, to a definition of the permissible limits of nonperfusion of the anoxic arrested heart at open-heart surgery, and to a determination of the maximal allowable transport time for cardiac transplantation. The factors in the myocardial cellular environment that support cellular viability and help maintain homeostasis are reviewed. Reversible surgically induced anoxic arrest is contrasted with the irreversible arrest and cell necrosis which often attend the myocardial anoxia of coronary occlusion. The enhancement of glycolysis, other changes in carbohydrate metabolism, and the depressed oxidation and lipid storage associated with alterations in lipid metabolism are outlined and their interrelationships discussed. The effect of the myocardial tissue acidosis which accompanies ischemic metabolism is an important factor in determining the reversibility of the effects of ischemia. The probable role of myocardial acid hydrolases in pathological ischemic autolysis is described. A sequence of cellular events induced by ischemia and leading to ultimate cell death is outlined. Promising areas for future investigation into the pathogenesis of myocardial infarction and into improved methods of treatment are suggested.</jats:p>

papers.title: Rod-derived cone viability factor 2 for the treatment of inherited retinal blindness
papers.authors: Zheng Li
papers.abstract:
<jats:title>Rod-derived cone viability factor 2, un traitement des dégénérescences rétiniennes héréditaires</jats:title>
                <jats:p xml:lang="fr">La rétinite pigmentaire (RP) est la forme la plus répandue de maladies rétiniennes héréditaires (IRDs), caractérisée par une dégénérescence progressive des photorécepteurs en bâtonnets, suivie d'une perte secondaire des cônes, menant à une altération de la vision puis à la cécité. Actuellement, il n'existe pas d'options thérapeutiques définitives pour la rétinite pigmentaire avancée. Cette thèse vise à étudier le potentiel thérapeutique du rod-derived cone viability factor-2 (RdCVF2), codé par le gène NXNL2, en association avec RdCVF, codé par son paralogue NXNL1, pour le traitement de la RP. Le gène NXNL1 code deux isoformes : RdCVF, qui soutient la survie des cônes, et RdCVFL, qui atténue le stress oxydatif. De manière similaire, NXNL2 produit RdCVF2 et RdCVF2L, impliqués dans le maintien rétinien et dans des fonctions neuronales plus larges.Pour explorer l'interaction entre ces gènes, nous avons généré des souris double knock-out (Nxnl1-/-Nxnl2-/-) et comparé leur phénotype rétinien avec celui des knock-outs simples (Nxnl1-/- et Nxnl2-/-) ainsi que des témoins de type sauvage. Les double knock-outs présentaient des déficits structurels et fonctionnels plus sévères, soulignant les rôles non redondants de Nxnl1 et Nxnl2 dans le maintien des photorécepteurs.Parallèlement, nous avons évalué le potentiel thérapeutique de l'administration combinée de RdCVF et RdCVF2. Des études in vitro sur des cultures rétiniennes enrichies en cônes ont montré que le co-traitement améliorait la survie des cônes, légèrement plus que chacun des facteurs administré seul, suggérant un effet synergique possible. Pour évaluer l'efficacité thérapeutique in vivo, RdCVF et RdCVF2 ont été administrés par injection sous-rétinienne médiée par AAV2/8 dans le modèle murin rd10 de rétinite pigmentaire. Toutefois, aucune amélioration significative de la fonction ou de la structure rétinienne n'a été observée. L'analyse de l'expression du rapporteur GFP a révélé une transduction variable et sous-optimale, indiquant que l'inefficacité de la délivrance génique a probablement limité les effets thérapeutiques.En résumé, ce travail met en évidence les contributions distinctes et complémentaires de Nxnl1 et Nxnl2 au maintien rétinien et propose une base pour l'utilisation combinée de RdCVF et RdCVF2 dans une approche thérapeutique indépendante du génotype pour la RP. Bien que le potentiel thérapeutique demeure prometteur, une optimisation supplémentaire des stratégies de délivrance génique ainsi qu'une exploration approfondie du mécanisme d'action de RdCVF2 sont nécessaires pour envisager une application clinique effective dans le traitement de la RP.</jats:p>

papers.title: PRC2 is high maintenance
papers.authors: Jia-Ray Yu; Chul‐Hwan Lee; Ozgur Oksuz; James M. Stafford; Danny Reinberg
papers.abstract: As the process that silences gene expression ensues during development, the stage is set for the activity of Polycomb-repressive complex 2 (PRC2) to maintain these repressed gene profiles. PRC2 catalyzes a specific histone posttranslational modification (hPTM) that fosters chromatin compaction. PRC2 also facilitates the inheritance of this hPTM through its self-contained "write and read" activities, key to preserving cellular identity during cell division. As these changes in gene expression occur without changes in DNA sequence and are inherited, the process is epigenetic in scope. Mutants of mammalian PRC2 or of its histone substrate contribute to the cancer process and other diseases, and research into these aberrant pathways is yielding viable candidates for therapeutic targeting. The effectiveness of PRC2 hinges on its being recruited to the proper chromatin sites; however, resolving the determinants to this process in the mammalian case was not straightforward and thus piqued the interest of many in the field. Here, we chronicle the latest advances toward exposing mammalian PRC2 and its high maintenance.

papers.title: In vitro phospholipid biosynthesis for growing and dividing minimal cells
papers.authors: Scott, A.D.D.
papers.abstract: Natural life is extraordinarily complex, which by definition means that it has many interconnected and functioning parts. The goal of synthetic biology is to engineer living systems, though due to their very complexity they remain recalcitrant to engineering. What if it were possible to reduce the complexity to a finite amount of parts that are well understood and therefore possible to manipulate. That is the motivation for constructing a so called minimal cell.
papers.categories: Synthetic biology; Natural (archaeology); Biology; Cell biology; Computer science

papers.title: Asymmetric Division of Damaged Proteins in Proliferating Cells
papers.authors: Mary Rose Bufalino
papers.abstract: This thesis explores the unequal partitioning of damaged proteins during mitosis and its implications for cell fate. Initially described in unicellular organisms, it was unclear if this method was used in vivo in multicellular organisms and had functional consequences in mammalian cells. To determine if this asymmetry was conserved in multicellular organisms, I studied three stem/progenitor populations in Drosophila: the larval neuroblast, adult female germline stem cell, and adult intestinal stem cell. Each cell type was found to asymmetrically segregate damaged proteins identified by the 2,4-hydroxynonenal (HNE) modification, which are associated with oxidative stress and age. Both the larval neuroblast and female germline stem cell were found to retain damaged proteins during division, whereas the intestinal stem cell segregated damaged proteins to differentiating progeny. I suggest that functional lifespan, and not cell type, determines the cell that receives the majority of damaged proteins during division. In each cell type, damaged proteins were associated with DE-Cadherin, a common component of the stem cell niche and removal from the niche was associated with reduced damaged protein polarization. Interestingly, when larval neuroblasts were mechanically dissociated from their niche and placed in culture, the internal polarization of damaged proteins was found to increase with progression through the cell-cycle. Therefore, I suggest that both the niche and intrinsic factors play a role in the asymmetric division of damaged proteins. To determine if an asymmetric division of damaged proteins influenced cell fate, I used a mammalian cell line with inducible expression of misfolded Huntingtin, which shares similar properties to damaged proteins. This study also revealed that the conformation of damaged proteins impacts cell fate: cells with diffuse Huntingtin displayed greater proliferation and reduced resistance to stress. Tracking cells containing an aggregate with live-imaging revealed that the cell that inherits the aggregate has a longer cell-cycle and an enhanced capacity to differentiate. Therefore, the asymmetric inheritance of damaged proteins impacts cell fate. In the final chapter of this thesis, I discuss the implications of an asymmetric division of damaged proteins on cell fate and how this information can be applied to cancer treatments.
papers.categories: Division (mathematics); Cell division; Cell biology; Biology; Genetics

papers.title: The immune boundaries for stem cell based therapies: problems and prospective solutions
papers.authors: Abdelkrim Hmadcha; Domínguez‐Bendala Juan; Jane A. Wakeman; Arredouani Mohamed; Bernat Soria
papers.abstract: Introduction Classification and sources of stem cells Limitations of stem cells Alternatives to overcome the limitations of stem cells Histocompatibility and immune rejection Are ESCs immunogenic or immunoprivileged? Overcoming the need for immune manipulation to avoid rejection Manipulating immune tolerance for stem cell‐based therapies Conclusions Stem cells have fascinated the scientific and clinical communities for over a century. Despite the controversy that surrounds this field, it is clear that stem cells have the potential to revolutionize medicine. However, a number of significant hurdles still stand in the way of the realization of this potential. Chiefly among these are safety concerns, differentiation efficiency and overcoming immune rejection. Here we review current progress made in this field to optimize the safe use of stem cells with particular emphasis on prospective interventions to deal with challenges generated by immune rejection.
papers.categories: Stem cell; Immune system; Intensive care medicine; Immune reaction; Medicine

papers.title: Cell Cycle-dependence of cisplatin-and carboplatin-induced dna damage
papers.authors: Sangamitra Villalan
papers.abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapeutic drugs such as cisplatin and carboplatin induce intra- and interstrand crosslinks, resulting in replication arrest, and cell death. Translesion synthesis by DNA polymerase eta, is one way in which human cells can tolerate platinum-induced adducts. Because these adduct block replication, the cell cycle stage at the time of drug exposure, and the DNA polymerases expressed could affect the outcome of exposure. The aim of this research was therefore to investigate the effects of cell cycle phase at the time of drug exposure on cell viability, cell cycle progression and activation of DNA damage responses in pol eta-deficient (XP30R0) and pol eta-expressing (TR30-2) human fibroblast cell lines. Using nocodazole arrest and release to generate populations of cells enriched in G1, S or M phases, it was found that XP30R0 cells in S-phase were more sensitive to drug treatment compared to cells that were in G1- and M-phase at the time of treatment. When G1 cells were treated with drug, cell arrest in S- and G2/M-phases was detected by flow cytometry. When S-phase XP30R0 cells were treated with cisplatin, a strong S-phase arrest was detected, however, when treated with carboplatin, arrest in S phase was less pronounced, and there was evidence for S-phase arrest in a second cell cycle. In TR30-2 cells, the extent of S-phase arrest was less than in XP30R0 cells, consistent with a role for pol eta in replication of damaged DNA. In M-phase XP30R0 cells following treatment, cells were delayed entering S and by 24 hours post-treatment, strong S-phase arrest occurred. Using western blotting and immunofluorescence, it was found that DNA damage-induced phosphorylation of key PIK kinase substrates including H2AX, Chk1 and RPA2, was induced following drug treatment of XP30RO cells in all cell cycle phases. Comparison of the timing of Chk1 ser317 and RPA2 ser4/ser8 phosphorylation demonstrated that activation of the Chk1 phosphorylation was an earlier event than RPA2 phosphorylation, independent of the cell cycle phase at the time of exposure. RPA2 phosphorylation was consistent with prolonged replication arrest in S-phase cells. Using small molecule inhibitors, roles for DNA-PK and CDK1/2 in damage-induced RPA2 phosphorylation were identified. The data provides an insight into the molecular events that determine the outcome of drug exposure in cells treated at different phases of the cell cycle, and may be relevant to identification of pathways that can be targeted to improve the efficacy of these drugs in cancer therapy.
papers.categories: Carboplatin; Cisplatin; DNA damage; DNA repair; DNA

papers.title: The Role of Atypical E2fs in the Maintenance and Development of the Ependymal Cell Barrier
papers.authors: Delphie Dugal-Tessier
papers.abstract: The discovery of neural stem cells within the adult CNS has indicated an enormous potential in facilitating neuronal regeneration after injury. Studies from our laboratory have suggested that manipulation of the Rb/E2f pathway can directly impact embryonic and adult neurogenesis, thereby having tremendous potential for neuronal regeneration therapies. Recently, two new members of the Rb/E2f pathway have been discovered, the atypical E2fs: E2f7 and E2f8. Initial studies have suggested that atypical E2fs regulate diverse processes such as cell proliferation, DNA-stress response, apoptosis, however, their importance in the brain are unknown. To analyze their function during brain development, we crossed Nestin-Cre mice with mice bearing a conditional E2f7/E2f8 allele to delete both E2f7 and E2f8 in neural precursor cells. Whereas cortical development was largely unaffected by E2f7/E2f8 deficiency, we observed an enlargement of the lateral ventricles occurring postnatally, a brain condition named ventriculomegaly. We then looked at the ependymal cells, which are the cells lining the wall of the lateral ventricles, to determine if these cells were affected by the absence of atypical E2fs. We found progressive denaturation of the ependymal cell layer, distortion of the ependymal motile cilia and reactive astrocytes within the layer. We identified Gli3, a component of the Sonic hedgehog pathway (Shh), as a target for E2fs, including atypical E2fs. We unravelled a novel mechanism by which atypical E2fs regulate the expression of Gli3, leading to up-regulation of Numb/NumbL, which in consequence destabilizes cadherins organization within the ependymal cell layer. In conclusion, our work suggests that E2f7 and E2f8 transcription factors play an essential role in maintaining the ependymal cell barrier.

papers.title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
papers.authors: Vladimir Juričić; Rodrigo Soto-Garrido
papers.abstract: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

papers.title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
papers.authors: Viraj Agrawal; Kirankumar Shiragur
papers.abstract: Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $α$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN's slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{α+1}{α-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $γ> 0$, showing a $\tfrac{2}γ$ approximation on navigable graphs ($α\approx 1$), where greedy search admits no guarantees. In this work, we unify and generalize these results by proving that ABS with parameter $γ$ on $α$-reachable graphs achieves an approximation of $\tfrac{α+1}{α(γ+1)-1}$ for any metric. Moreover, on sorted $α$-reachable graphs (introduced by Gollapudi et al.) under the $\ell_2$ metric, we obtain the tighter bound $\max\bigl(\tfracα{α(γ+1)-1}, \tfrac{α^{2}+1}{α^{2}(γ+1)-1}\bigr)$. Beyond these theoretical results, we design a beam predictor using features inspired by fine-grained analysis of ABS, trained via a constrained objective that minimizes mean distance computations subject to a target recall. On three 100-million-point benchmarks, using graphs built by DiskANN's practical construction, beam predictor lowers mean query latency on SSD-resident indices at matched recall by up to $29.6\%$ relative to classical beam search (CBS). Relative to ABS, it is faster in $11$ of $15$ settings, by up to $6.5\%$, and at most $1.4\%$ slower in the other $4$; at $95\%$ recall, its advantage over ABS grows from $0.8$--$4.2\%$ for $100$ neighbors to $4.6$--$5.6\%$ for $500$ neighbors. In memory, it needs $1.3$--$23.7\%$ fewer distance computations than CBS and $0.0$--$3.9\%$ fewer than ABS.

papers.title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
papers.authors: David Halpenny; Adithya Sireesh; Petros Wallden
papers.abstract: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art. We show that in-place modular multiplication of integers, modulo a power of two, can be performed with either a classical or quantum odd multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$. We then show that standard in-place integer multiplication can be performed with a non-zero classical or quantum multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates for any $ε>0$, with no ancilla qubits required for the classical multiplier and a logarithmic number of ancilla qubits for the quantum. Using our quantum modular multiplication algorithm, we also show that in-place modular inversion, modulo a power of two, can be performed using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$. To our knowledge, these are the first quantum algorithms achieving both subquadratic gate counts and sublinear ancilla counts for each of the considered in-place operations. All but one of these fast operations are optimal in terms of memory, only requiring enough space to store the output of the operation, which overwrites the input directly. We present our multiplication algorithms as consequences of a single unified theorem, which may find further application within quantum arithmetic.

papers.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
papers.authors: Peiyun Hu; Marko Mihajlovic; Lyndon Duong; Lahav Lipson; Wei Dong; Amaël Delaunoy; Stephan R. Richter; Vladlen Koltun
papers.abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

papers.title: Local orbital magnetization and Chern markers from equilibrium local currents
papers.authors: Henrique P. Veiga; Aires Ferreira; Caio H. Lewenkopf; João M. Viana Parente Lopes
papers.abstract: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. However, producing realistic simulated images of local currents in inhomogeneous systems remains challenging. Building upon recent work on stochastic estimation methods for tight-binding models, we show that all matrix elements of positive semidefinite operators defined on a lattice can be obtained at once from a single set of filtered random vectors. This eliminates the need for independent simulations previously required for off-diagonal elements, which significantly speeds up the calculation of spatial maps of local currents. Further, we express bond currents in terms of loop currents that obey a discrete Poisson equation, with the current vorticity acting as the source term. Its solution yields a local orbital magnetization. In analogy with the global Středa relation, the derivative of this magnetization with respect to the chemical potential defines a new local Chern marker. Built entirely from bond currents, it requires no position operator and is not bound by the zero-sum rule of projector markers in open samples. Hence, it is free of boundary-compensation artifacts, and its sample average converges to the bulk Chern number in a controlled fashion.

papers.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
papers.authors: John M. Martyn; Rod Rofougaran; Samuel Stein; Di Luo
papers.abstract: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

papers.title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
papers.authors: Rami Atar; Leonid Mytnik; Dominic T. Schickentanz
papers.abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

papers.title: Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
papers.authors: Yuanyuan Li; Xianduo Wang; Xu-jia Wang
papers.abstract: We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.
